title: Cross-arbitration: moving a service
summary: The machine arbitrator never moves a task: it asks the cluster (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25). ClusterArbitrator~planMoves(now, access) places each ServicePlacement by its rules (zone, optional GMT window, minimum share of access; first match wins, else the home zone) and minimum residence. XTP addresses services, not equipment (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25), so a move is ROUTE_SERVICE: the target XTP daemon registers the service address and the route is published (LDAP); clients keep the address. Only a DNS edge names equipment and needs REPOINT_DNS and WAIT_DNS; a GATEWAY edge never changes. FABRIC state: activate on the target, CHECK_SERVING, route, (DNS), then release the old copy, so both serve during the overlap. CHECKPOINT state: deactivate first, activate on the target, check, route; the outage is stated. TEMPORARY state does not move. A target must take the service without asking the cluster anything, else the service stays and the decision says why.
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: Clients address the service, never a machine
A new copy is checked before anyone is routed to it
The old copy goes only after the route has moved (and old DNS answers have expired)
procedure: Treat the cluster answer and the quorum decision as events; call planMoves or muDown again
